items.title: nixos/nixos-generate-config: reoder LUKS and LVM

items.content_html:
Previously, if virtual devices (like LVM logical volumes) were contained within a LUKS device, mounting the virtual device would not pull in the hardware config to decrypt the LUKS device (when using the script to generate the hardware config). This would cause the OS to not decrypt the LUKS device and be unable to mount the currently mounted device after the next boot. Now, we will recursively search for any LUKS devices that needs to be decrypted in order to mount the device.

Fixes #490144

items.content_html:
Partially fixes #27789 by using matching devices found in /dev/disk/by-label/* before using any found in /dev/disk/by-uuid/*.

Wil T's install tutorial explains the motivation: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=axOxLJ4BWmY&t=1295s

Description of changes

This doesn't change any packages; only newly generated hardware configurations are affected.

This does NOT fix #27789 as originally reported (I was not able to repro that myself), but does address this comment.

At some point the automatic detection of device labels broke and device UUIDs began taking precedent over labels. This makes setting up a new computer a more manual and error-prone process than it needs to be.

With this change, I can instead use the devices generated as-is in hardware-configuration.nix on reinstall.

Motivation: Having a shorter /etc/ssh/sshd_config, thus making it easier to audit.

Since we default to upstream's defaults, we can safely default these to null.

Per https://man.openbsd.org/sshd_config :

  • LogLevel default is INFO.
  • UseDNS default is "no".
  • X11Forwarding default is "no".
  • PermitRootLogin default is "prohibit-password".
  • KbdInteractiveAuthentication default is "yes".
  • GatewayPorts default is "no".
  • StrictModes default is "yes".

#? 7
Please select a country whose clocks agree with yours.
 1) Åland Islands	 18) Greece		   35) Norway

14) Finland		 31) Monaco		   48) Turkey
15) France		 32) Montenegro	   49) Ukraine
16) Germany		 33) Netherlands	   50) Vatican City
17) Gibraltar		 34) North Macedonia
#? 47

The following information has been given:

	Switzerland
	Büsingen

Therefore TZ='Europe/Zurich' will be used.
Selected time is now:	Tue Dec  5 15:24:52 CET 2023.
Universal Time is now:	Tue Dec  5 14:24:52 UTC 2023.

2) No

You can make this change permanent for yourself by appending the line

to the file '.profile' in your home directory; then log out and log in again.

Here is that TZ value again, this time on standard output so that you
can use the /run/current-system/sw/bin/tzselect command in shell scripts:

It's not great how it says to set it in .profile, but the NixOS docs should be obvious that it should be set to time.timeZone.

Summary

Telemt - MTProxy for Telegram on Rust + Tokio.

This PR:

  1. Adds me as a maintainer
  2. Adds the missing custom license

The package alone isn't useful without a systemd service to run telemt as a system service.

  • Declarative settings generates config and the service runs
  • Imperative configFile uses the provided file and the service runs
  • Assertion fires when the module is misconfigured

items.content_html:
Description

Add a new NixOS module for synchronizing kernel patches from lore.kernel.org.

Features

  • Periodic sync from kernel mailing list archives via public-inbox
  • Support for 14 kernel subsystems:
    • dri-devel - DRM/Graphics
    • netdev - Networking
    • linux-fsdevel - Filesystems
    • linux-mm - Memory management
    • linux-security-module - LSM
    • linux-hardening - KSPP hardening
    • rust-for-linux - Rust kernel development
    • linux-block, linux-btrfs, linux-ext4, linux-xfs - Storage
    • linux-usb, linux-pci - Hardware
  • Optional public-inbox/lei support for full mbox archives
  • Fallback to Atom feeds for lightweight sync
  • Automatic index generation
  • Full systemd hardening (DynamicUser, sandboxing)

Motivation

Kernel developers and security teams need to track upstream patch discussions. This module provides an automated way to sync patches from lore.kernel.org, the official Linux kernel mailing list archive.

Example Usage

Basic setup:

services.lore-sync = {
  enable = true;
  subsystems = [ "linux-hardening" "rust-for-linux" ];
};

Full configuration:

services.lore-sync = {
  enable = true;
  subsystems = [ "dri-devel" "netdev" "rust-for-linux" ];
  interval = "6h";
  lookbackDays = 14;
  useLei = true;  # Use public-inbox for full mbox
};

Use Cases

  • Kernel developers tracking patch discussions
  • Security teams monitoring hardening patches (KSPP)
  • Anyone following Rust-for-Linux development
  • Maintainers tracking filesystem/driver patches

Checklist

  • Module follows nixpkgs conventions
  • Options have descriptions and examples
  • systemd service is hardened (DynamicUser, sandboxing)
  • Added to nixos/modules/module-list.nix
  • Documentation (can add if requested)
  • NixOS test (can add if requested)

Related

  • lore.kernel.org: https://lore.kernel.org/
  • public-inbox: https://public-inbox.org/
items.title: nixos/lore-sync: init

items.content_html:
Description

Add a new NixOS module for automated CVE synchronization from the NIST National Vulnerability Database (NVD).

Features

  • Periodic CVE data fetching from NVD API 2.0
  • Incremental sync with state tracking (only fetches modified CVEs)
  • CPE-based product filtering (e.g., filter for Linux kernel CVEs only)
  • Automatic kernel CVE extraction for security monitoring
  • Full systemd hardening (DynamicUser, sandboxing, restricted syscalls)
  • Optional API key support for higher rate limits

Motivation

Security-conscious NixOS users and organizations need visibility into CVEs affecting their systems. This module provides the foundation for CVE awareness by fetching authoritative data directly from NIST NVD.

Example Usage

Basic setup:
```nix
services.nvd-sync = {
enable = true;
extractKernelCves = true;
};
```

With API key:
